statement: The Court held that the Eleventh Amendment prevents Congress from authorizing suits by Indian tribes against States to enforce legislation enacted under the Indian Commerce Clause, so a tribe could not use 25 U.S.C. 2710(d)(7) to sue a State for failing to negotiate in good faith. The Court also held that Ex parte Young could not be used to enforce 2710(d)(3) against a state official.
citation: Seminole Tribe of Fla. v. Florida, 517 U.S. 44 (1996)
title: Seminole Tribe of Florida v. Florida
quote: The Eleventh Amendment prevents Congress from authorizing suits by Indian tribes against States to enforce legislation enacted pursuant to the Indian Commerce Clause.

nations_as_named: Rincon Band of Luiseno Mission Indians of the Rincon Reservation
statement: The court affirmed the finding that California negotiated in bad faith by conditioning expanded class III gaming rights on a percentage-of-revenue payment to the state general fund; it held that general-fund revenue sharing is not a permissible subject under 2710(d)(3)(C)(vii) and that the offered exclusivity was not a meaningful concession. The district court order to conclude a compact or submit last best offers to a mediator was made effective.
citation: Rincon Band of Luiseno Mission Indians v. Schwarzenegger, 602 F.3d 1019 (9th Cir. 2010)
title: Rincon Band of Luiseno Mission Indians of the Rincon Reservation v. Schwarzenegger
quote: We AFFIRM the district court’s finding that the State of California negotiated with Rincon in bad faith by conditioning its agreement to expand Rincon’s class III gaming rights

statement: The en banc court affirmed summary judgment for the tribe on its claim that California failed to negotiate in good faith, holding that the State's challenge to the trust acquisition and tribal status was an improper collateral attack on BIA decisions. The opinion was amended by order of July 8, 2015.

title: Big Lagoon Rancheria v. California (en banc)
quote: The en banc court affirmed the district court’s summary judgment in favor of a tribe that alleged that the State of California had failed to negotiate in good faith for a gaming compact

statement: The court affirmed on different grounds, holding that when a State negotiates for compact provisions well outside IGRA's listed subjects it has not acted in good faith, and directed the parties to IGRA's remedial process. It explained that the "meaningful concessions" framework applies only to demands for taxes, fees or other revenue sharing.

title: Chicken Ranch Rancheria of Me-Wuk Indians v. California

statement: The court held that the State's challenge to the Secretary's Class III gaming procedures regulations (25 C.F.R. pt. 291) was ripe, that Texas had standing, and that the Secretary lacked authority to promulgate the regulations; it called the Secretarial procedures invalid and an unreasonable interpretation of IGRA. Opinion revised Sept. 13, 2007; Judge Dennis dissented.

title: Texas v. United States (Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas, intervenor)
quote: the case is ripe, the State has standing, and the Secretary lacked authority to promulgate the regulations.

statement: The court affirmed the district court: it held the 25 C.F.R. pt. 291 regulations are not a valid exercise of the Secretary's authority because they are foreclosed by IGRA's text, and that IGRA's jurisdiction-granting clause is severable after Seminole Tribe.
citation: New Mexico v. Dep't of the Interior, Nos. 14-2219 & 14-2222 (10th Cir. Apr. 21, 2017)
title: State of New Mexico v. Department of the Interior (Pueblo of Pojoaque, intervenor)
quote: we conclude that the Part 291 regulations are not a valid exercise of the Secretary’s authority

This is the "meaningful concessions" decision later applied in Rincon.

title: In re Indian Gaming Related Cases (Coyote Valley Band of Pomo Indians v. California)
quote: the district court's order denying Coyote Valley's motion is AFFIRMED.

A mediator later selected the tribe's last best offer and Interior issued Secretarial procedures in 2016.

quote: Defendant and Plaintiff are ordered to proceed pursuant to the remedial process set forth in the IGRA, 25 U.S.C. § 2710(d)(7)(B)(iii)–(vii).
